breaking_changes: The /v1/models/{model}/options endpoint's resolved_ctx_size field can now be null instead of always numeric when automatic context sizing cannot fit a valid context — clients parsing it as an integer will fail.
GET on previously-404 POST-only paths (slots/{id}, jobs/{id}/pause|interrupt|resume, models/register) now returns 405 instead of 404.

A request without the model field now raises 'Missing model field in request' consistently on every model route (chat/completions, completions, embeddings, responses, rerank), instead of the old inconsistent error messages.
Form-encoded requests with invalid field types (e.g. non-numeric temperature on transcription) return 400 instead of 500.
Streaming responses now carry a cancel token that stops the server from sending after a TCP disconnect.

evidence.blockers: The GUI3 desktop app has no evidence of manual end-to-end exercise by a human — the primary user-facing artifact ships with six new workspaces. The resolved_ctx_size null API change is unverified on a release candidate build and could break existing clients. The Windows ROCm sd-cpp path-length refusal and router configuration-error handling have not been manually tested. The NPU safety-guard follow-up from the 128 GB Strix Halo regression fix is still deferred.
evidence.breaking_changes: Five documented breaking changes ship in this release: resolved_ctx_size can be null (clients must handle non-integer), four POST-only routes now return 405 instead of 404, missing model field errors are now consistent across all model routes, form-field type conversion errors return 400 instead of 500, and streaming responses now cancel on TCP disconnect. Clients consuming these endpoints should audit their error handling. The /v1/models endpoint gains checkpoint_status[], update_available, and an opt-in include_paths query parameter — these are additive but existing clients that ignore unknown fields should continue working.
evidence.coverage: Reviewed the full range from v2026.43.3 to the release head (47 commits across PRs 3762–3989). Coverage spans server refactor (route-class architecture, model manager rewrite), GUI3 desktop launch, micro-features (microphone dictation, browser key persistence, chat history defaults), backend support (Windows ROCm, GRG-Halo, K2-Horizon models), API changes (resolved_ctx_size null, output_index in responses, checkpoint_status, model-sources endpoint), CI/workflow fixes, documentation, and a blog post. No gaps identified in the commit review evidence.
evidence.manual_testing: The full GUI3 interface across all six workspaces (Chat, Models, Backends, Apps, Monitor, Settings) needs end-to-end exercise with a running server — no human has done this. The API key persistence restoration in the web GUI (Remember API key checkbox and removal) needs verification against a release build due to localStorage security implications. Windows ROCm sd-cpp loading on Strix Halo hardware must be validated. The 128 GB Strix Halo regression fix (gpt-oss-120b, Qwen3-Next-80B, Qwen3-Coder-Next loading) should be re-checked on target hardware. Microphone dictation across five capability modes has only been self-tested by the author.
evidence.security: API key persistence was restored to browser localStorage (web GUI) with documented same-origin XSS warning; desktop clients remain isolated to native settings. The model delete fix reads actual disk state instead of trusting the JSON catalog, reducing trust in potentially stale catalog data. The Model Manager refactor improved HTTP redirect handling (custom headers cut at cross-origin boundaries). The Windows ROCm DLL staging mitigates DLL hijacking by placing known-good AMD runtimes alongside the executable. No new supply-chain risks, credential handling changes, or unexpected network calls observed.
